title: [Auckland] Reimagining Technology Careers in the Age of AI
location: AUT Auckland CBD campus, WG Building, WG126, Auckland
description:
AI is changing how technology is built, how organisations operate, and what skills businesses value. Rather than focusing on AI technology itself, this event will explore a more personal question:
**What does the AI era mean for our careers in the IT industry?**

CITA and BA Career will bring together four senior technology and business leaders to share their perspectives on how careers, skills and leadership may evolve over the next 5–10 years.

Moving beyond the technology itself, our panel will explore how AI is reshaping the technology workforce, how professional roles and career pathways may evolve, and what individuals and organisations can do to prepare for the changes ahead.

Whether you're a software engineer, business analyst, product professional, QA specialist, data practitioner, technology leader, or someone aspiring to enter the IT industry, this conversation will offer valuable perspectives to help you navigate your next career move.

### **Panelist**

* [Francis Ho](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ACoAAAw8JG4B-JrgunVhXl6GTGvJYA9Bvz6RT7g/?utm_source=chatgpt.com), Director of Engineering at Auror
* [Sylvia Ding](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ACoAAACqP5sBgkv85jGQhxjG4L9l08CxqjrvFTM/?utm_source=chatgpt.com), Advisor and Coach at LumenCo
* [Abinesh Krishan](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ACoAAACrBtUB_4Zd7UeaepF3SXbXCQgBNG1G8Lw/?utm_source=chatgpt.com), Chairperson of the Board at Potentia
* [Nathan Wallace](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ACoAAAUvOx4BncKVSOsFryu8WqrdRNtnQdxtYIA/?utm_source=chatgpt.com), Head of Digital Technology Operations at Millennium Hotels and Resorts

### **Facilitator**

[Kelly Hou](https://www.linkedin.com/in/kellyhou-nz/?utm_source=chatgpt.com), Head of Product Engineering at EverCommerce

title: AI Video Workshop: Make Your Marketing Video
description:
**By popular request, we're trying a *workshop* format. It will be hands-on so numbers are limited.**

We'll work through making AI marketing videos with you, on your own personal marketing projects. Bring images, assets, copy and any other materials for your product or brand, and we'll help you build with them during the session.

There's no fixed pipeline. Depending on what you're making, we'll look at the approaches that suit your project, from image-to-video and reference-driven generation to editing, sound and finishing.

Places are capped at 20 so everyone gets hands-on time and attention on their own work.

What to bring:

* Your laptop
* Product images, website links and brand assets
* Copy, scripts or a rough idea of the story you want to tell
* The tools you already use, if you have any

**IMPORTANT- the workshop is free but if you want hands-on experience generating your own video you'll need a video generation service. For experimentation, we recommend Google Flow for this session, https://flow.google.com. There is a free plan for students, and it's super cheap otherwise for the first month which will give you plenty of time to play.**

No prior experience needed. If you're curious about AI video for marketing and want to get your hands on a real project, this is for you.

Afterwards we usually continue over dinner nearby, a good chance to connect with fellow builders and practitioners.

title: Build Night: Demos, Collabs & Open Source in Practice
description:
A fortnightly, hands-on session focused on the projects the Auckland AI Collective is actually building — together.

Each session centres on **demonstrations** of what members are working on. Expect live demos, group experiments, and the occasional "let's just try it and see what happens" moment — so come ready to get involved, not just watch. Some parts may invite your participation; none of it is polished or precious.

The tone is **casual and informal**\- eat dinner\, drink\, and enjoy\. This is a place to share ideas\, get feedback\, find collaborators\, and turn "someone should build that" into an actual repo\.

What we cover will vary week to week depending on what people bring and what the group is curious about — the constant is the room: builders comparing notes and starting things together.

**This is for you if** you want to get directly and personally involved in group projects, collaborations, and **open source**.

See what we're already building on GitHub: [https://github.com/auckland-ai-collective](https://github.com/auckland-ai-collective)

Bring a project, a problem, an idea, or just yourself.

After this session we can hang out as long as we like at the restaurant if you want to keep the conversation going and connect with other professionals.

title: 0x29 Auckland Meetup at Plexure
location: 2 Graham Street, Auckland CBD, Auckland 1010, New Zealand, Auckland
description:
**WHAT TO EXPECT**
Join us for another Hack The Box meetup in Auckland! Whether you're thinking about being a hacker or are already a seasoned one, this event has something for everyone.

The event will include a guided walk through of an HTB machine, demonstrating essential tools and techniques for enumeration, exploitation, and privilege escalation. After the walk through, you'll have the opportunity to explore an additional HTB machine, collaborate with other members, and tackle various challenges together.

At the end, we will do a raffle where we will give out HTB prizes, such as VIP access to the platform and HTB Academy cubes.

This is an on-site event in Auckland CBD.

**WHAT YOU GET**

* A chance to win some HTB giveaways
* Access to our HTB dedicated lab during the event

**WHAT YOU NEED**

* A laptop.
* A HTB account.
* Discord application.

**HOUSE RULES**

* Follow all rules and guidelines in the **[HTB TOS: HTB Terms of Service](https://www.hackthebox.com/tos)**
* Active HTB content cannot be shared publicly. Retired challenges or machines are fair game.
* Plexure hosts the event to support the growth of the local cybersecurity community and to support students and professionals in their journeys to learn. Respect for the venue and people is expected from all attendees.

title: Welcome to the next AWS Auckland Well-Architected Meetup for 2026!
location: Level 13, Commercial Bay, 15 Customs Street West, Auckland CBD, Auckland 1010, Auckland
description:
Hi Architects,

Welcome to the next AWS Auckland Well Architected User Group Meetup of 2026!

At each meetup, we focus on learning and networking in a friendly and inclusive atmosphere and explore best-practices in AWS. This has resulted in the AWS Well-Architected Meetups becoming the most popular AWS Meetups in ANZ 🥳

**Please also note that AWS Security now requests a company name and company email where it is available. If you are a student, please list your institution and your student email address at that institution 👍**

We'll be announcing more speakers on [https://well-architected.me](https://well-architected.me/) and previewing presentations during the coming weeks - our speakers and details this month include:

* **Michael Taylor, Lakebase Specialist, Databricks**

**How Lakebase provides a well-architected platform for next generation application and AI development.**
Come and hear how Databricks experts show how customers run applications and agents on Lakebase; serverless Postgres governed by Unity Catalog. See instant branching, scale-to-zero, point-in-time recovery and synced tables in action. The Databricks team will also give a first look at LTAP; one open, governed copy of data for transactions and analytics, with no ETL in between.

* **Kristof Ringleff, Solution Architect, Fooman**

**From Weekend Project to Well-Architected: Putting AWS's new Well-Architected Agent to Work**

Kristoff had a small serverless weekend project running on AWS. So he pointed the brand-new AWS Well-Architected Agent at it. Then I did what any sensible engineer would do with a hobby app; I followed its advice. This talk covers what the agent found, what I learned along the way and the fun of over-engineering something that never needed it. I'll also compare it with the open-source Well-Architected Review skill, which runs in your own coding agent and needs no AWS Support plan.
